headline: Discussed draft FY2028 capital plan, a $2.4 million budget request including debt.
summary: The commission approved its previous minutes, then reviewed the draft plan with Public Works Director Jon Rauscher. The plan includes three equipment replacements added to debt and a $20,000 reserve for Parks grant matches. Finance Director Angela Aldieri said the plan may push debt past the city's 15% General Fund limit, which would need Council approval.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting minutes, moved by Brittany Nevins and seconded by Autumn Crabtree.
Commission agreed the draft plan seemed reasonable, especially the work on the water main.

plain_text:
11/10/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Cait Hoffman, Autumn Crabtree, Brittany Nevins, Jen Berger, and Elsie 
Goodrich. The Municipal Infrastructure Commission members present were Tom Buckley, 
Micayla Schambura, Eli Ogilvie, and Thea Wurzberg
City Staff Present: Angela Aldieri, Jon Rauscher
Guests Present:
Call to Order by: Cait Hoffman
Meeting Start Time: 6:01PM
Minutes Recorded by: Autumn Crabtree
Public Comment
There was no public comment
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Brittany Nevins
Second: Autumn Crabtree
Decision: Approved
City Council Liaison Update
Councilor Goodrich updated the committee on the ongoing work of City Council. They approved 
two new policies for city employees and there is an ongoing fundraiser campaign for the 111 
Weaver Fire Station Annex. The fundraiser is an effort to furnish two rooms for full time staff. 
The Burlington Airport Noise Mitigation Program continues. The FY2028 budget season has 
begun and with that the start of the public engagement project. Council had a joint meeting with 
the Winooski School District regarding a merger study required by Act 170 of 2026. The city 
continues to do an assessment on equitable housing needs. There is a new candidate for the 
finance commission who will be recommended to council. The Sugar House Hotel grand 
opening is happening and she encourages people to stop by.
Inclusion & Belonging Commission Update
Inclusion and Belonging Jen Berger updated that their last meeting did not happen due to a lack 
of a quorum. They have a new member and are interviewing others.
Discussion: Draft FY2028 Capital Plan Review
Director of the Public Works Department (PWD) Jon Rauscher gave the committee an 
overview of the FY28 Draft Capital Improvement Plan. He gave an overview of what the capital 
plan is, how capital assets and projects are selected, what the city’s existing capital assets are, 
ongoing capital improvements, and 2026 grant applications related to capital work. Many 
commission members questioned what improvements are planned to be made on Malletts Bay 
Avenue.
The commission then looked at the existing capital debt service and Director Rauscher walked 
through a spreadsheet outlining this. He then walked through the draft proposed FY28 Capital 
Plan for the General Fund. There are three large equipment replacements that will be added to 
the debt, and the rest of the budget is one time spending. This includes a $20,000 reserve for 
grant matches for the Parks Department. All in for FY28 (including debt) the budget request is 
$2.4 million. Director Rauscher showed the Commission the 5-year target street resurfacing 
plan and the fleet replacement that is outlined in the budget, including two that are included in the 
Sewer Fund and Water Fund budgets, respectively. The cost of sidewalk replacement and 
paving was discussed, as Eli asked what the plan is for sidewalk replacement in FY28. If there 
is staff time, the city will patch the sidewalk in sections. The city has experimented with other 
ways to fix sidewalks, but this was fairly expensive in relation to the correction. One issue with 
sidewalk replacement is a lack of data, which PDW is looking into improving.
Cait asked how the Finance Commission can be helpful in the discussion of the Capital Plan. 
Finance Director Angela Aldieri said that the best feedback is knowing if there is something in 
the community that they are missing or if there was anything surprising. She also wanted to 
highlight that a large part of the budget is debt, which makes it difficult for the city to invest in 
other projects. The city has a policy set by City Council that they are only allowed to take on 15% 
of the General Fund in debt, and this may place the city over this threshold, which means that 
they would be limited unless the Council approves going over. Brittany asked that the 
Commission be alerted when the public engagement process is happening, and how we can be 
more involved. Elsie said she will send out an email with the public engagement activities that 
are scheduled. The proposed budgets will be presented at City Council starting on December 
7th through the end of January. The Capital Plan and Public Works budget will be presented on 
December 14th. Jen said that the places planned for public engagement events, such as Specs 
and The Last Stop, have a specific demographic and asked how outreach may happen for 
people who do not frequent these places. Elsie suggested we circle back to this at our next 
meeting. The Commission agreed that the Plan seemed reasonable, especially the work on the 
water main. Cait asked how our debt policy compares to other municipalities across Vermont, 
and Angela said it is pretty middle of the road. A lot of Vermont municipalities do not have a 
policy like this due to our small size but Angela consulted multiple sources before the policy was 
set. Cait asked about the urgency of fixing the water main, and Jon said that PWD is in the 
process of designing a plan, and will start fixing the most urgent sections next year. Gretchen 
asked if there was anything that could be waited on, and Angela and Jon agreed that most things 
outlined in the budget are necessary in the next year.
Other Business
There was no other business.
Adjourn
Motion by: Brittany Nevins
Second: Autumn Crabtree
Meeting End Time: 7:19
I.
II.
III.
IV.
V.
VI.
VII.
VIII.
DRAFT
